deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is a list of research problems, one entry per line, from Hilbert's early problem notebook (c. 1885–88, Königsberg). Each entry is restated below in modern terms. Supplementary counts and arguments are marked [mine].

(0) Continuation of the previous page. The previous page asks when a prescribed chain of transvection (Überschiebung) processes can terminate. Hilbert notes that one then 'has to do with a group of operations'. He says examples occur among 'my irrational covariants', e.g. when the determining equation becomes reducible. This refers to his 1886/87 Math. Ann. paper on a general viewpoint in binary invariant theory, where irrational covariants arise from the roots of a determining equation.

(1) Notation: for binary forms φ, ψ of order 7, the 4th transvectant is (φ,ψ)_4 = Σ_{j=0}^{4} (-1)^j C(4,j) ∂^4φ/∂x^{4-j}∂y^j · ∂^4ψ/∂x^j∂y^{4-j}, up to a normalising constant.
- Claim: (φ,ψ)_4 = 0 determines, to a given φ, a covariant ψ uniquely.
- [mine] Counting: (φ,ψ)_4 has order 7+7-8 = 6, so it has 7 coefficients. It is bilinear in the coefficients of φ and ψ. For fixed φ it gives 7 linear homogeneous equations M(φ)·b = 0 in the 8 coefficients b of ψ.
- [mine] For generic φ, M(φ) has rank 7, so ψ is unique up to scale. Its coefficients are the signed 7×7 minors of M(φ). Hence ψ is a covariant of degree 7 in the coefficients and order 7.
- Because the transvectant index 4 is even, (ψ,φ)_4 = (φ,ψ)_4. So φ is in turn 'the' such covariant of ψ, as Hilbert says.
- [mine] Iterating, T(T(φ)) has degree 49 in the coefficients of φ. Since φ solves M(ψ)b = 0, generic uniqueness forces T(T(φ)) = I(φ)·φ, with I an invariant of degree 48.
- Hilbert asks what the vanishing of this invariant means. [mine] I = 0 means M(ψ) drops rank: the correspondence φ↔ψ fails to be an involution and ψ admits more than one partner.

(2) φ of order 10 with (φ,φ)_8 = 0.
- [mine] (φ,φ)_8 has order 20-16 = 4, so the condition imposes 5 conditions on the 11 coefficients. That leaves a 6-dimensional family.
- Modulo GL_2 (dimension 4) this leaves 11-5-4 = 2 essential parameters (moduli), matching Hilbert's 'only 2 undetermined parameters'.
- Task set: compute the complete system of invariants and covariants (vollständiges Formensystem) for such special decimics.

(3) Gordan's problem: write a sextic as square plus cube, f = c^2 + q^3, with c cubic and q quadratic.
- [mine] Count: 4+3 = 7 unknowns against 7 coefficients, so generically finitely many representations.
- Hilbert's proposed generalization: f = φ^m ψ^n + χ^σ ρ^r (more general binomial decompositions of a form into products of powers). He also writes the companion f' = φ'^m ψ'^n, presumably the degenerate case where one term is absent.

(4) Require (f, f∘T)_i = 0 for a binary form f and a linear substitution T.
- For i = 1 the transvectant is the Jacobian. [mine] For two forms of equal order, a vanishing Jacobian implies proportionality, so f∘T = c·f. This is exactly f admitting the transformation T into itself, as in Klein's polyhedral ground forms and Fuchs's forms attached to linear ODEs with algebraic solutions.
- The problem asks for the analogue for higher i.

(5) Re-prove the main theorem of his 1885 dissertation (invariant properties of special binary forms, in particular spherical-harmonic / Legendre-type forms) using infinitesimal transformations, i.e. Lie-algebra / Cayley–Aronhold differential operators.

(6) The 'Lagrange problem': solve F(x,y) = a x^n + b x^{n-1} y + … = 2^m in integers x, y (and m). In modern terms this is a Thue–Mahler equation with the single prime 2.
errors: No computational errors; the page contains only problem statements.
The count '2 parameters' for (φ,φ)_8=0 is right only if the 5 conditions are independent and one quotients by the 4-dimensional GL_2. This is implicit in Hilbert's 'also'.
Uniqueness of ψ in (1) holds only for generic φ (rank M(φ) = 7). Hilbert's follow-up question about the vanishing invariant shows he was aware of the exceptions.

results.modern_name: Apolarity-type (transvectant-orthogonality) correspondence; kernel covariant of a bilinear covariant map
results.usually_credited_to: General apolarity theory: Reye, Rosanes, Sylvester (1870s–80s); this specific case unsure

results.modern_name: Invariant theory of special binary forms defined by vanishing transvectants
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's own early research program (cf. his 1885 dissertation on special forms)

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); trans=lambda f,g,k: expand(sum((-1)**j*binomial(k,j)*diff(f,x,k-j,y,j)*diff(g,x,j,y,k-j) for j in range(k+1)))
checkable.asserts: Definition of the k-th transvectant (up to normalization), used below.

checkable.sympy: a=symbols('a0:8'); b=symbols('b0:8'); phi=sum(a[i]*x**(7-i)*y**i for i in range(8)); psi=sum(b[i]*x**(7-i)*y**i for i in range(8)); T=Poly(trans(phi,psi,4),x,y); len(T.coeffs())==7 and degree(T.as_expr().subs(y,1),x)==6
checkable.asserts: (φ,ψ)_4 for order-7 forms has order 6, giving 7 bilinear conditions on ψ's 8 coefficients.

checkable.sympy: M=Matrix([[diff(c,bj) for bj in b] for c in Poly(trans(phi,psi,4),x,y).coeffs()]); M.subs({a[i]:randint(-5,5) for i in range(8)}).rank()==7
checkable.asserts: For generic φ the linear system has rank 7, so ψ is unique up to scale.
Even transvectants are symmetric, so the φ↔ψ relation is symmetric.

checkable.sympy: c=symbols('c0:11'); f=sum(c[i]*x**(10-i)*y**i for i in range(11)); P=Poly(trans(f,f,8),x,y); len(P.coeffs())==5
checkable.asserts: (φ,φ)_8 for a decimic has order 4: 5 conditions; 11-5-4(GL2)=2 moduli.

checkable.sympy: Matrix([[diff(e,ci) for ci in c] for e in P.coeffs()]).subs({c[i]:randint(-5,5) for i in range(11)}).rank()==5
checkable.asserts: The 5 conditions are generically independent, so the solution variety has dimension 6.

checkable.sympy: u=symbols('u0:4'); v=symbols('v0:3'); cub=sum(u[i]*x**(3-i)*y**i for i in range(4)); q=sum(v[i]*x**(2-i)*y**i for i in range(3)); F=Poly(expand(cub**2+q**3),x,y); Matrix([[diff(e,s) for s in u+v] for e in F.coeffs()]).subs({s:randint(-5,5) for s in u+v}).rank()==7
checkable.asserts: Sextic = square of cubic + cube of quadric: the parameter map 7→7 is generically of full rank, so there are finitely many representations.
